summary_en: ITG-G Holdings launched a tender offer for all Kadoya Sesame Mills shares at 2,514 yen per share from September 15 to October 30, 2026. The minimum acquisition target is 13,847,100 shares (66.65% of outstanding shares post-3-for-1 split). The board approved the bid and recommended shareholders tender, with the company planning to delist after the acquisition.
title_en: Notice of Tender Offer for Ordinary Shares of the Company by ITG-G Holdings Corporation and Recommendation to Tender
translation_en_brief:
ITG-G Holdings Corporation, established on July 17, 2026, and wholly owned by Integral Corporation (an equity investment firm), has launched a tender offer to acquire all outstanding ordinary shares of Kadoya Sesame Mills at 2,514 yen per share. The offer runs for 30 business days from September 15 to October 30, 2026. The minimum number of shares to be acquired is 13,847,100 shares, representing 66.65% of the company's outstanding shares (calculated based on 276,213 voting rights, which accounts for a 3-for-1 stock split executed in April 2026). Following the acquisition, the company plans to be delisted and transition to a private entity.

The Kadoya Sesame Mills board of directors unanimously approved the tender offer on September 14, 2026, and recommended shareholders tender their shares. The board's decision was based on the company's assessment that the transaction would maximize shareholder value and corporate value. The approval was granted through a voting process excluding directors and auditors with conflicts of interest. The transaction contemplates that only ITG-G Holdings, Ozawa Bussan Co., Ltd. (third-largest shareholder), Ozawa Shoji Co., Ltd. (fourth-largest shareholder), and Kazuhiko Ozawa (founder and shareholder, with controlling interests in Ozawa Bussan and Ozawa Shoji) will remain as shareholders following completion of the acquisition and delisting.

While the company and a special committee have prioritized discussions with ITG-G Holdings, they stated that evaluation of proposals from other potential buyers remains ongoing and that any new or revised proposals will be carefully considered. The board's decision was made with the understanding that completion of the delisting process would follow the successful conclusion of the tender offer.
